headline: Monday Night Football: Chargers visit Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium in Harbaugh Bowl
teaser: Brothers Jim and John Harbaugh clash under the prime-time lights in Baltimore as Justin Herbert and the physical Chargers test Lamar Jackson and the explosive Ravens.
story:
Week 10 of the NFL season wraps up with a marquee Monday Night Football spectacle on 16 November, as Jim Harbaugh leads his Los Angeles Chargers into M&T Bank Stadium to take on brother John Harbaugh and the Baltimore Ravens.

The iconic coaching rivalry adds extra intrigue to a matchup with massive AFC playoff ramifications. The Chargers enter at 6-3, boasting one of the league's stingiest scoring defenses behind pass rusher Joey Bosa and safety Derwin James, while Justin Herbert continues to pilot an efficient run-first attack anchored by J.K. Dobbins.

Standing in their path is two-time MVP Lamar Jackson and a Baltimore offense averaging over 29 points per contest. Jackson and running back Derrick Henry present the ultimate test for Los Angeles' front seven in what promises to be a physical, 60-minute battle for postseason seeding.
whyCareReason: The high-profile Harbaugh Bowl pits brother against brother with major AFC wild card and division race implications under the Monday Night Football spotlight.
stakes: A victory secures a vital head-to-head tiebreaker in the ultra-competitive AFC playoff hierarchy.
rivalryAngle: Jim Harbaugh and John Harbaugh face each other for the first time since Super Bowl XLVII, reigniting the NFL's premier sibling coaching rivalry.
funFacts: Jim and John Harbaugh previously coached against each other in Super Bowl XLVII in February 2013.
Lamar Jackson is 23-6 in prime-time regular-season games throughout his NFL career.
The Chargers defense enters allowing just 14.8 points per game, the third lowest in the NFL.
